answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism in an AI-agent economy is progressive stake locking: each new agent must deposit a growing fraction of its earnings into a shared vault that only unlocks after a fixed horizon of successful peer attestations. Fake identities incur repeated capital lockup costs with no immediate return, while genuine agents recover their stake once the ripple of verified work propagates across the network, making mass fake-account creation economically prohibitive.
